absent: Numeric values of address layout constants, PARAM_SIZE, COMMAND_LINE_SIZE, descriptor selectors, and control register masks.
Full layout of boot_params and boot header fields beyond version and hardware_subarch.
Page table entry formats, fixmap slot assignment, and encryption mask application.
GDT and IDT descriptor layouts and exact early handler table linkage.
Semantics of platform quirks, microcode load, sanitizer init, and trampoline setup beyond call sites.
APIC MMIO and MSR address values and complete SMP bringup protocol.

findings.text: The 64-bit C boot entry receives firmware boot data location, enforces image layout at build time, establishes early CPU and memory state, copies firmware data into resident structures, installs the high mapping slot from the early top table, and transfers control to reservation setup without returning.

The reservation entry re-copies firmware data when version indicates absence, applies platform quirks, dispatches Intel MID early setup based on hardware subarchitecture, then enters generic kernel initialization without returning.

Firmware boot data handling creates temporary decrypted views when memory encryption is active, copies a fixed parameter block into resident storage, sanitizes it, conditionally copies command line only when its pointer is nonzero into a fixed resident buffer, then tears down temporary views so no decrypted mapping remains.

64-bit assembly startup preserves the firmware data pointer across calls, establishes a known stack and per-CPU base, installs early descriptor state, normalizes code segment, optionally enables memory encryption before feature probes, sanitizes CPU configuration, derives relocation offset, applies page table fixups, switches to the early top table, and branches to shared startup at its virtual address.

Secondary and common 64-bit startup sanitizes CPU state, clears stale firmware pointer on secondaries, switches to the initial top table while dropping identity mappings, preserves a narrow control subset while cycling global paging to flush global translations, resolves CPU number via control word or APIC lookup, establishes per-CPU stack and descriptor and segment state, configures system call and no-execute controls, normalizes control register and flags, and calls the registered initial code pointer.

32-bit entries initialize flat segments and stack, clear resident uninitialized data, copy firmware parameters and command line before paging is usable, create early page tables and fixmap wiring, then join a shared path that normalizes control and flags, probes CPU identity and paging extensions, enables paging, collects vendor and family and capability identity, finalizes control state, installs protected mode descriptors and segments with empty LDT, and calls the registered initial code pointer.

Early exception coverage provides a uniform per-vector stub table that normalizes missing error codes with a dummy value, records vector number, and funnels to a common handler which builds a full register frame, normalizes data segments, dispatches by vector to fixup logic, then restores state and returns from interrupt while tracking recursion.

Early fault paths guard reentry with a counter; nested interrupt while reporting forces a halt loop, failed CPU identity lookup releases the trampoline guard and halts with interrupts disabled, and control never falls through after dispatch to C code because a trapping instruction follows the call.

A single shared guard word coordinates real mode trampoline use; it is tested for null on the boot processor, cleared after a CPU obtains its own stack, and cleared before halting when CPU identity lookup fails, with no other synchronization in these fragments.

When five-level paging is enabled the kernel switches page offset and dynamic mapping and memory map bases to five-level variants before clearing uninitialized data and top table state, and encryption initialization precedes any faulting operation while global TLB invalidation follows sanitizer initialization due to instrumented control register access.

Secondary CPU identification uses a control word where one high flag selects APIC discovery and low bits carry CPU number for single bringup, with X2APIC detection and ID fetch from MMIO or MSR forms, matched against a firmware supplied APIC to CPU table bounded by configured CPU count.

Early IDT installation optionally establishes a confidential computing host communication block and selects a dedicated boot exception vector handler before loading the IDT; the dedicated handler builds a register frame, forwards frame pointer and vector to a registered C handler, unwinds, discards error code, and returns from interrupt.
Soft restart reloads the current task stack pointer from per-CPU current state and rejoins the common jump to registered initial code without reestablishing paging or descriptor state.

Resident firmware copies use fixed extents named by PARAM_SIZE and COMMAND_LINE_SIZE with command pointer offset NEW_CL_POINTER, and early handler tables use fixed counts and strides named by NUM_EXCEPTION_VECTORS and EARLY_IDT_HANDLER_SIZE with error code presence mask EXCEPTION_ERRCODE_MASK.
